Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur | IIT KGP
72nd Convocation
4th July 2026
(the date is subject to minor change based on availability of Guests)
ABOUT IITKGP
Dedicated to the service of the Nation
The motto of IIT Kharagpur is "योगः कर्मसु कौशलम्". This literally translates to "Excellence in action is Yoga", essentially implying that doing your work well is (true) yoga. This can be traced to Sri Krishna's discourse with Arjuna in the Bhagavad Gita. The quote, in the larger context of the Gita, urges man to acquire equanimity because a mind of equanimity allows a man to shed distracting thoughts of the effects of his deeds and concentrate on the task before him. Equanimity is the source of perfection in Karmic endeavours that leads to Salvation.

The institution generally mentions "Catalyzing Careers" as part of its overall mission.

ACADEMIC PROGRAMS AND DEPARTMENTS

Indian Institute of Technology Madras offers a variety of academic programs including Undergraduate Programmes, Postgraduate Programmes, and Research Programmes. New Academic Programmes are announced for 2026. The institution also offers International Students Academic Programs. There is an Online BSc Programme which is a completely online program aimed at creating a trained programmer proficient in application development, data sciences, and machine learning. The B Tech programmes at IIT Madras encourage interdisciplinary studies and cater to the changing scientific and technological needs. Postgraduate programmes are specialized programs aimed at engaging students in learning, teaching, and research. Research Programmes are internationally renowned for their quality and diversity, offering opportunities for active research in frontier areas. An International Masters’ Program (I2MP) is offered, with courses aimed at bringing students with diverse interests to the IIT Madras campus and providing them the benefit of the rich teaching and research environment. IIT Madras encourages collaborations with foreign universities through student exchange programmes and visiting faculty. The institution is at the forefront of collaborative learning and research, having Joint Ph.D. programs with 20 world-class institutions. IIT Madras is inviting applications for Web-Enabled M.Tech and PG Diploma Programs. Admissions are also open for a 4 year Medical Science and Engineering Program. UG Programme Admissions 2025 and PG Programme Admissions 2025 are announced. The DDWS Innovation Challenge 2025 - 26 application portal is currently open, and a Summer Fellowship 2026 is also announced.

The institution comprises the following departments:
The Department of Aerospace Engineering was established in 1969 and stands at the forefront of fundamental and applied research. The Department of Applied Mechanics & Biomedical Engineering has grown significantly since its inception in 1959. The Department of Biotechnology was founded in 2004 with a strong interdisciplinary research and teaching base. The Department of Chemical Engineering aims to be a global center of academic and research excellence in chemical engineering sciences and technology. The Department of Chemistry is one of the first departments to function after IIT Madras was founded in 1959. The Department of Civil Engineering has grown into a full-fledged department since its inception in 1959. The Department of Computer Science & Engineering was conceived in 1973 with the acquisition of an IBM System/370, which was one of the most powerful computers in India at that time. The Department of Electrical Engineering is actively involved with research from absolute fundamentals and component levels. The Department of Engineering Design was established in 2006 and is noted as the first of its kind in India. The Department of Humanities and Social Sciences (HSS) is one of the oldest departments at IIT Madras. The Department of Management Studies was established in 2004 to accommodate the popular Master in Business program. The Department of Mathematics was established in 1959 along with the Institute and has taken the responsibility of teaching. The Department of Mechanical Engineering is the largest of its kind in the country and one of the largest in Asia. The Department of Metallurgical and Materials Engineering is one of the oldest, having been started in the same year as the Institute. The Department of Ocean Engineering (DOE) was originally conceived as the Ocean Engineering Centre (OEC) in 1977. The Department of Physics is amongst the largest physics departments in the country in terms of the number of faculty members.

Information about the academic calendar, semester system, credit system, grading system, minimum attendance requirements, examination pattern, special programs, honors courses, minor degrees, electives offered, curriculum, course structure, or recent changes to academic programs is not explicitly detailed in the provided content.

FACULTY AND ACADEMICS

Indian Institute of Technology Madras has a total of 591 Faculty members. The specific breakdown into professors, associate professors, and assistant professors is not provided. The percentage of faculty members with PhD degrees is not mentioned. The student to faculty ratio can be calculated from the provided numbers: there are 2,105 Undergraduate Students, 4,112 Postgraduate Students, 746 MS Research Scholars, and 2,963 PhD Research Scholars, totaling 9,926 students. With 591 faculty members, the student to faculty ratio is approximately 16.79 students per faculty member.

Prof. V. Kamakoti is the Director of the institute. The Director acknowledges the continuing efforts of all faculty members, students, and staff in maintaining the institute's distinguished position. The institution emphasizes the significance of a campus in ensuring quality learning and aims to infuse it with a spirit of inclusivity, celebrating pluralism of cultures, nationalities, and personalities. The campus is envisioned to reflect the ethos of innovation, entrepreneurship, and dynamism of spirit. Each IITian is encouraged to foster an endless, restless quest for solutions to real-world problems, contributing to society and helping the nation achieve self-reliance (atma-nirbhar). The Director envisages the presence of IIT Madras to be felt far beyond the campus walls, making a tangible difference to society with leading innovations and determined efforts.

The teaching methodology is implied to be rigorous, engaging students in learning, teaching, and research, with a focus on quality learning. Research opportunities for students are highlighted as active in frontier areas. Faculty accessibility is not explicitly detailed, but the Director's message suggests a collaborative environment where faculty, students, and staff work together towards excellence.

RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT

Indian Institute of Technology Madras is internationally renowned for the quality and diversity of its research, offering opportunities for active research in frontier areas. The institution has 146 Patents and has undertaken 829 Projects.

Notable research highlights include a study by IIT Madras scientists on "How cool motorbikes are choking Indian cities!" which shows the polluting impact, and research on "Why getting too personal may harm e-Commerce!"

The institution houses several research centers and laboratories:
The Centre for Technology and Policy (CTaP) provides analyses. The Centre for Railway Research (CRR) was set up in 2015 to develop railway-related technologies. The Centre of Excellence in Wireless Technology (CEWiT) was established with support from the Ministry of Communication and IT. The Healthcare Technology Innovation Centre (HTIC) is another key center. The TTK Center for Rehabilitation Research and Device Development (R2D2) focuses on rehabilitation research and device development. The National Technology Centre for Ports, Waterways and Coasts (NTCPWC) is dedicated to ports, waterways, and coasts. The National Centre for Combustion Research and Development (NCCRD) was founded by the Combustion Institute – Indian Section and receives support from various entities. The Advanced Manufacturing Technology Development Centre (AMTDC) focuses on advanced manufacturing. The Indo-German Centre for Sustainability (IGCS) was established in 2010. The International Centre for Clean Water (ICCW) was established in 2018 with the objective of creating water professionals. The Centre for Computational Brain Research (CCBR) is a high-level research center. The IITM China Studies Centre was established in April 2011. external.text:
The Indian Institute of Technology Madras, often referred to as IIT Madras or IITM, is a public institute of technology situated in Chennai, Tamil Nadu, India. Established in 1959 with technical, academic, and financial assistance from the government of West Germany, it holds the distinction of being the third Indian Institute of Technology to be founded. IIT Madras is recognized as an Institute of Eminence and an Institute of National Importance by the Government of India. The institute is a residential campus spanning 620 acres (2.5 square kilometers), much of which is a protected forest carved out of the adjoining Guindy National Park, home to diverse wildlife including chital, blackbuck, and monkeys. The campus also features a natural lake, which was deepened in 1988 and 2003, and drains most of its rainwater. As of 2021, the institute had an endowment of ₹700 crore (US$93.26 million) and a budget of ₹996 crore (US$100 million) for 2021-2022. The academic staff comprises 674 members, serving a student body of 10,238, which includes 4,909 undergraduates, 2,488 postgraduates, and 2,841 doctoral students.

PLACEMENTS

The placement scenario at IIT Madras is consistently strong, attracting top recruiters and providing excellent career opportunities. The institute has a dedicated Career Development Cell that focuses on the all-around preparation of students for the placement process. The recruitment process typically commences in July and concludes in May, with registration starting in August. Pre-Placement Talks and aptitude and technical tests are usually conducted between September and November.

For the 2024 placement season, a total of 1,091 students secured placements across Phase I and Phase II. By April 30, 2024, over 80% of B.Tech and Dual Degree students and 75% of Master's students had been placed. A total of 256 companies participated in the placement process. The average package for the 2024 batch was INR 22 LPA, and the median package stood at INR 19.60 LPA. The highest package at IIT Madras Placements 2024 reached INR 1.31 crore per annum. There were 44 international job offers made to students. Additionally, out of 300 Pre-Placement Offers (PPOs) extended, 235 were accepted. Approximately 40% of students were hired in Core Engineering roles, while 20% secured positions in Software. Other popular sectors included Finance, Consulting, and Data Science.

In the 2023 placement drive, 1,612 job offers were made by over 480 companies. The highest salary package for B.Tech students in 2023 was INR 1.31 crore per annum. For M.Tech students, the highest package in 2023 was INR 54.21 LPA. The median salary for MS (Engineering Streams) was INR 15 LPA, and for MSc (Science Streams), it was INR 9.62 LPA. MA graduates received a highest package of INR 26.57 LPA, while MBA graduates secured offers up to INR 30.66 LPA. PhD students received packages up to INR 35.89 LPA.

For the 2023-24 placement season, the median CTC was ₹19.6 LPA and the average CTC was ₹22 LPA. There were 35 international offers from recruiters from the US, Japan, and other countries. A total of 183 startup offers were also made.

The Department of Management Studies (DoMS) at IIT Madras also reported 100% placements for the batch of 2023-2024. The highest CTC for DoMS reached INR 29.65 LPA, with an average CTC of INR 16.93 LPA. The median CTC for MBA students in 2024 was INR 16.39 LPA. The top 25% of MBA graduates achieved an average CTC of INR 21.89 LPA. In the 2024 MBA placements, 445 job offers were made, and 407 pre-placement offers were recorded. Notably, 25 candidates received packages exceeding INR 1 crore per annum, and 15 international offers were made. A total of 331 companies participated in the MBA placement drive. The breakdown of offers included 172 offers exceeding INR 30 LPA, 48 offers in the INR 25-30 LPA range, 135 offers between INR 20-25 LPA, and 312 offers between INR 15-20 LPA.

Year-wise placement statistics:
For 2023-24, the average salary for core engineering roles, including mechanical, was around INR 15 LPA.
In the 2023-24 placement season, 1,091 students were placed, with an average package of INR 22 LPA and a median package of INR 19.60 LPA.
For the 2022-23 and 2023-24 academic years, IIT Madras alumni and CSR partners ensured financial support for 100% of B.Tech students with an annual parental income between Rs 1 lakh and Rs 5 lakh.
In December 2023, during Phase I of placements, approximately 50% of students were placed, with over 55% of placed students coming from socially and economically weaker backgrounds. The median salary offered in Phase I of IIT Madras placements 2023 was over Rs 19 lakh.

Top recruiters at IIT Madras include Google, Amazon, Microsoft, JP Morgan Chase, Adobe, Intel, Flipkart, ITC Ltd., Deloitte, EY India, and Texas Instruments. Other prominent recruiters mentioned for 2023-24 include Goldman Sachs, McKinsey & Company, Qualcomm. For MBA placements, American Express, Cogoport, Linecraft AI, and SAP Labs were prominent recruiters.

Student reviews indicate that IIT Madras provides excellent placements, shaping careers in engineering, research, and other fields.

Internship Placements:
IIT Madras has updated its B.Tech curriculum to include six-month internships. In the internship drive for the 2023-24 batch, there was a 19% increase in internship offers on the first day. Students received 19 international internship offers from seven foreign companies. The number of students who received internships increased by 17%, and the number of firms that visited the campus increased by 51%. Major recruiters in the internship drive included Texas Instruments, JP Morgan Chase and Co, Adobe, Procter and Gamble, and Dr Reddy's Laboratories.

ACADEMICS AND CURRICULUM

IIT Madras is globally recognized for its rigorous academic curriculum, world-class faculty, and state-of-the-art laboratory facilities. The institute offers a wide array of undergraduate, postgraduate, and doctoral programs across 16 academic departments and several advanced research centers. Student reviews describe IIT Madras as transformative, with top-notch academics.

Programs Offered:
The institute offers a four-year B.Tech program, which is highly sought after.
For the academic year 2025-26, two new B.Tech programs have been introduced through the Department of Applied Mechanics and Biomedical Engineering, accessible via JEE Advanced and JoSAA counseling: B.Tech in Computational Engineering and Mechanics (CEM) and B.Tech in Instrumentation and Biomedical Engineering (iBME). The B.Tech in Computational Engineering and Mechanics (CEM) program bridges traditional engineering with modern computational methods, AI, and data science, preparing graduates for roles in aerospace, robotics, and sustainable energy. The B.Tech in Instrumentation and Biomedical Engineering (iBME) is an interdisciplinary program integrating biomedical, electrical, and instrumentation engineering, aimed at developing next-generation medical devices and healthcare technologies. Both programs offer an upgrade path to a five-year dual degree through Interdisciplinary Dual Degree (IDDD) programs.

Beyond JEE, IIT Madras has launched other programs:
A four-year B.S. in Chemistry (from 2025-26) with an upgrade option to M.S. in Chemistry, with admission through the IISER Aptitude Test. Students can pursue a minor degree in Data Science or allied fields and undertake project work across engineering departments.
An M.Tech in Electric Vehicles (from 2025-26), a postgraduate program preparing engineers for the rapidly growing EV sector, with admission through GATE.

For the 2026-27 academic year, IIT Madras is launching a wide range of new undergraduate, postgraduate, online, and web-enabled academic programs. These programs span diverse fields such as Mathematics, Robotics, Semiconductor Materials Technology, Public Policy, Sustainable Engineering, Offshore and Maritime Engineering, Sports Analytics, and AI.
Key launches include a new four-year B.S. Program in Mathematics by the Department of Mathematics, which offers students the option to continue for an additional year and graduate with a dual B.S.-M.S. degree. This program will offer electives related to Cryptography, Computational Mathematics, Quantitative Finance, Financial Engineering, Actuaries, Data Analytics, AI-enabled Manufacturing, and Quality Engineering. Students can also pursue minors in complementary disciplines.
A new M.Tech in Semiconductor Materials Technology is focused on next-generation fabrication, aiming to prepare graduates for roles such as Process Engineers, Yield Enhancement Specialists, and Materials Scientists.
An M.A. in Public Policy seeks to equip students with a deeper understanding of governance, policy design, and public administration across sectors like healthcare, education, environment, transportation, finance, and international relations.
Other new M.Tech programs include Robotics and Process Safety. The M.Tech in Robotics focuses on the design, analysis, and application of advanced robotic systems across industrial and societal contexts, with extensive coursework and significant project work in state-of-the-art laboratories.
New M.Sc courses include Sustainable Engineering and Sports Analytics.
New B.S. degrees are also being introduced in Aeronautics and Space Technology and Management and Data Science.

Curriculum Quality:
The institute constantly strives to update its curriculum to align with evolving industry needs, equipping students with the necessary skills to excel in their chosen careers. Reports indicate that IIT Madras has updated its B.Tech curriculum to include six-month internships.

Academic Rigor and Pressure:
Life at IIT Madras blends academic rigor with a vibrant hostel culture. However, some student reviews indicate that academics can be overwhelming.

Faculty Quality:
IIT Madras is known for its world-class faculty. Overall, the faculty at IIT Madras plays a crucial role in maintaining the institution's reputation for excellence in education and research. Some student reviews, however, mention inconsistent faculty quality.

E-learning Platforms:
IIT Madras has launched three new artificial intelligence courses through the SWAYAM Plus platform as part of the 'AI for All' campaign. These courses aim to make digital skills accessible to a wider audience, including those without a technical background. The new courses include AI for Aspiring Engineers, AI for Administrators, and Prompt Engineering. The AI for Aspiring Engineers course is priced at Rs 500 plus GST, while the other two courses are available at Rs 100 plus GST each. The SWAYAM Plus platform, which has completed two years, now offers over 500 courses across 15 sectors, with over 5.5 lakh learners registered.

RANKINGS AND RECOGNITION

IIT Madras has consistently secured the top position in the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) rankings, particularly in the 'Engineering' and 'Overall' categories, making it a highly sought-after destination for engineering aspirants. It has been ranked #1 in the 'Engineering' category for the 10th consecutive year in NIRF 2025 and in the 'Overall' category for the 7th consecutive year. IIT Madras has held the #1 rank in the Engineering Category every year since the NIRF Rankings were introduced.

NIRF Rankings:
NIRF 2025:
Overall: Rank 1
Engineering: Rank 1
Research Institutions: Rank 2
Management: Rank 13
Innovation: Rank 1 (improved from #2 last year)
Sustainability Development Goals (SDG): Rank 1 (new category)

NIRF Score Breakdown (2025):
Overall score: 87.31 (marginally higher than the previous year's 86.42)

International Rankings:
QS World University Rankings 2026: 180th globally. This marks a significant jump of 47 places from its 227th rank in 2025. It is the third-highest ranked Indian institution in this global list.
QS World University Rankings 2024: 227th globally.
QS Asia University Rankings: 74th.
Academic Ranking of World Universities (ARWU) 2022: 701-800 in the world.
QS WUR Ranking By Subject: =29.

EduRank 2026: 5th in India, 536th globally. For Engineering, it ranked 4th in India and 248th in the World. For Physics, it ranked 4th in India and 275th in the World.

Government Recognition:
IIT Madras is recognized as an Institute of National Importance by the Government of India. It was established by the Government of India through an Act of Parliament.

Other Rankings and Awards:
Outlook India ranked IIT Madras 1st among government engineering colleges in 2022.

FEES STRUCTURE

IIT Madras provides a structured fee waiver program and scholarships to assist students from financially weaker sections of society. Financial constraints are not intended to hinder students from studying at IIT Madras, as the institute has a layered system of fee waivers, government scholarships, alumni-funded support, and research stipends.

Tuition Fees and Waivers for B.Tech and Dual Degree Students:
Students whose annual parental income is below ₹1 lakh per year receive a full 100% tuition fee waiver, along with an annual scholarship of ₹40,000. A Women's Merit Scholarship of ₹10,000 per year is also available within this category.
For students in the ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh annual income bracket (EWS/GE/OBC category), the Merit-cum-Means (MCM) Scholarship, combined with the Government of India's two-thirds tuition fee waiver, covers the entire tuition fee. This means students from families earning up to ₹5 lakh a year can study at IIT Madras with zero tuition fees.
Students from SC/ST categories are entirely exempted from paying tuition fees, regardless of their parental income. They are also granted free messing and a monthly pocket allowance of Rs 250.
The Merit-cum-Means Scholarship is awarded to up to 25% of the sanctioned intake in each program, based on academic merit and financial need (family income below ₹4.5 lakh per year). IIT Madras alumni and CSR partners have ensured that 100% of B.Tech students in the ₹1 lakh to ₹5 lakh income category received financial aid for two consecutive years (2022-23 and 2023-24). The scholarship per student in this category is Rs. 66,667, disbursed in two halves per academic year.
To maintain eligibility for the Institute Free Studentship and SC/ST Scholarship, students must achieve a minimum GPA of 5.0 each semester.

Fee Waivers for Online Degree Programs:
For online degree programs, fee waivers are designed to help financially disadvantaged students.
Students with a family income above 5 LPA are not eligible for fee support.
Students with a family income between 1 and 5 LPA are eligible for 50% fee support.
Students with a family income below or equal to 1 LPA are eligible for 75% fee support.
For the General Category, an EWS certificate is required for fee support.
For the OBC Category, an OBC-NCL certificate is required.
SC/ST and PwD categories are eligible for 50% fee support at all income levels, and 75% fee support if income is ≤1 LPA with the respective certificate.

Other Scholarships:
Merit-based scholarships are also available.
The Institute Notional Prize is awarded to 7% of admitted students based on JEE rank and parental income below Rs 4.5 lakh, providing a one-time grant of Rs 1,000.
The Girish Ready Scholarship is granted to students with the highest JEE rank or exceptional all-round performance in school, with a family income below Rs 5 lakh, providing Rs 25,000 per year. Renewal is subject to a minimum GPA of 8 in the previous semester.
Scholarships sanctioned by NCERT, Central, and State governments are also provided to meritorious B.Tech students. The Tamil Nadu Scholarship is provided by the Directorate of Backward Class/Directorate of Most Backward class.
Students admitted to the M.Tech program through GATE are awarded Half-Time Teaching Assistantships (HTTA) at ₹12,400 per month.
M.Sc students receive ₹1,000 per month under the merit scholarship.
Full-time PhD scholars also receive financial assistance.

Hostel Fees and Mess Charges:
Hostel facilities are available for both male and female students. There are 20 hostels in total, with 15 for males and 5 for females. First-year undergraduates are provided sharing-style accommodation, while senior undergraduates may receive single, double, or triple rooms depending on the hostel. Postgraduate students have options for sharing or single rooms.

STUDENT LIFE AND CAMPUS CULTURE

Life at IIT Madras is described as a blend of academic rigor with a vibrant hostel culture, technical fests, and student clubs. The lush green campus offers a serene and conducive environment for learning and research. The campus is home to a diverse ecosystem of flora and fauna, including blackbucks and spotted deer.

Hostel Life:
Hostel facilities at IIT Madras are generally well-regarded for their quality and support to student life. The hostels offer comfortable accommodation with various amenities, including Wi-Fi, study areas, and recreational facilities. Rooms are typically equipped with basic furniture, providing a conducive environment for both study and relaxation. Hostels have 24x7 internet connection, TV, sports areas, gyms, laundry services, and mess facilities. There are 15 hostels for boys and 4 for girls, with single, double, or triple sharing rooms. These hostels are facilitated with internet connectivity, washing machines, and common rooms.
Student reviews on Quora mention individual single rooms with 24-hour internet access and 1 GB high-speed net access, along with unlimited GB of hproxy net. DC++ is also a popular feature for entertainment. Rooms typically include a cot, a fitted almirah, a fan, a table, and a chair. Common washrooms are cleaned daily. Some hostels allow the entry of girls into boys' hostels from 9 AM to 7 PM, with discretion lying with the warden. All hostels have common rooms with televisions.
Mandakini is the male freshie hostel, consisting only of shared rooms (two-person or three-person). It is known for its height, views, and amenities such as multiple laundry rooms in every wing of every floor, badminton courts, reading rooms, and common rooms. Cauvery Hostel is considered the sophomore hostel, known for its comfort and amenities, including multiple playgrounds, mini football fields, a batting cage, and laundry rooms. Brahmaputra is another sophomore hostel, smaller in size but known for the closeness and camaraderie of its residents. It is undergoing renovations and contains a well-maintained kitchen and music room. Alaknanda is the hostel closest to the Taramani Gate. Ganga and Jamuna hostels have been recently renovated, offering updated washroom facilities and more amenities. Godavari is also a recently renovated hostel, located near the Himalaya Mess and Food Court. Narmada Hostel, while perhaps not yet renovated, is renowned for its passionate cultural representation in inter-hostel events and is located opposite the Rotterman Food Truck, offering cheap food options late at night. Saraswati Hostel is renovated, clean, and well-equipped, located opposite Quark (which includes Zaitoon and a hangout spot) and facing the Sangam grounds.

Mess Food:
Specific complaints or praises about mess food are not extensively detailed in the provided snippets, but the presence of a Himalaya Mess and Food Court near Godavari hostel is mentioned.

Ragging and Discipline:
Information regarding the ragging situation and discipline is not explicitly detailed in the provided search results.

Safety on Campus:
Information regarding campus safety for all genders is not explicitly detailed in the provided search results. However, a Quora answer mentions that for hostel entry and exit at night, one needs to provide information to guards for records, which is primarily for safety.

Social Life and Cultural Diversity:
The hostel life at an IIT is described as creating lifelong nostalgic memories with many friends. The time spent with peers, including discussions, late-night walks, and multiplayer games, is considered among the best and most important parts of studying at an IIT. The campus is home to a diverse ecosystem of flora and fauna.

Technical and Cultural Festivals:
IIT Madras hosts various technical and cultural festivals. The Sports Fest is an intercollegiate meet for local colleges in sports like tennis, volleyball, basketball, hockey, football, table tennis, weightlifting, and badminton, held every September. The institute also hosts two major All India Inter Collegiate Tournaments for Boys and Girls: the GF&KR All India Invitational Basketball Tournament and the Jimmy George Tournament for Volleyball. The Sanmar Tournament for Cricket is another prestigious event. The Dean's Trophy, held in the even semester, includes events like six-a-side football, bridge, chess, and cycling. Various departments also have their own sporting events, often played at Sangam under floodlights. Gymkhana Day marks the culmination of all sports activities for the academic year.

Sports Facilities and Culture:
IIT Madras offers world-class sports facilities. These include multiple stadia, indoor and outdoor courts, gyms, a swimming pool, and specialized grounds for cricket, football, hockey, and athletics.
Specific facilities include:
Volleyball mud courts near the Sports Complex.
Basketball concrete courts near the volleyball courts.
Tennis court taff courts near the basketball courts.
A swimming pool complex with shallow and deep pools.
The KS Narayanan Centre for Cricketing Excellence (Chemplast Ground).
Football and hockey grounds.
A skating and multipurpose ground (Sangam).
Manohar C Watsa Stadium, an athletic field with a 400m synthetic track.
The IIT Gymkhana Complex houses weightlifting, a fitness center, a squash court, and a yoga hall.
The Sitara Indoor Sports Complex, inaugurated on November 4, 2024, is a new addition, contributed by an anonymous alumnus. It features four advanced badminton courts, several table tennis courts, a mezzanine floor supporting a gallery, and an open tennis court on the terrace.
Other facilities include a fully-stocked gym with professional trainers, a weightlifting arena, a massive stadium, a high-tech wood-floored multipurpose indoor stadium in the Students' Activity Centre, four synthetic-floored tennis courts, wood-floored badminton courts, two world-class squash courts, two basketball courts, two volleyball courts, hockey and football fields, and a table tennis facility. A new complex is under construction for more indoor sports. Hostels also have grounds and indoor courts for casual playing.

IIT Madras boasts world-class infrastructure and facilities, offering abundant opportunities to students. The campus is clean and green.

Classrooms, Labs, and Teaching Facilities:
The institute has over 40 laboratories, which are well-equipped with modern technology and equipment. There are various well-furnished and regularly maintained science labs, engineering labs, and space labs available at certain departments.

Library:
IIT Madras has a central library that is well-equipped with academic resources and modern facilities. The central library contains a huge amount of printed books, journals, and theses. The digital library provides access to a considerable number of online databases, e-books, e-journals, CD-ROMs, and reports. Student reviews praise the central library as top-notch and well-stocked.

Internet Connectivity:
The institute provides a high-speed internet connection across the campus. According to student reviews on Quora, the speed reaches up to 95 MBPS. Hostels also have 24x7 internet access. Student reviews mention 1 GB high-speed net access and unlimited GB of hproxy net in hostels. Wi-Fi is generally reliable throughout the campus.

Sports Infrastructure:
IIT Madras offers world-class sports facilities, including multiple stadia, indoor and outdoor courts, gyms, a swimming pool, and specialized grounds for cricket, football, hockey, and athletics. RECENT NEWS AND DEVELOPMENTS

New Programs and Academic Initiatives:
For the academic year 2026-27, IIT Madras is launching a wide range of new undergraduate, postgraduate, online, and web-enabled academic programs in fields such as Mathematics, Robotics, Semiconductor Materials Technology, Public Policy, Sustainable Engineering, Offshore and Maritime Engineering, Sports Analytics, and AI.

New M.Tech programs include Semiconductor Materials Technology, Robotics, Process Safety, and Mechanical Engineering with Specialisation in Computational Engineering for Mechanical Systems (CEMS).
New M.Sc courses include Sustainable Engineering and Sports Analytics.
A new M.A. in Public Policy has also been introduced.
From 2025-26, two new B.Tech programs, Computational Engineering and Mechanics (CEM) and Instrumentation and Biomedical Engineering (iBME), have been added through JoSAA.
A B.S. in Chemistry (from 2025-26) and an M.Tech in Electric Vehicles (from 2025-26) have been launched through other entry routes.

The School of Sustainability was launched in October 2023.

Professor V. Kamakoti is the Director of IIT Madras.

COMMON PRAISES FROM STUDENTS

Students and alumni consistently praise IIT Madras for several key aspects. The overall life at IIT Madras is described as great and phenomenally transformational. The institute is lauded for its top-notch academics and world-class faculty. The campus environment is a significant point of praise, often described as lush green, serene, and conducive for learning and research. The hostel facilities are well-regarded for their quality, comfort, and amenities, including 24x7 internet access, study areas, and recreational facilities. The availability of individual single rooms with high-speed internet is particularly appreciated. The central library is consistently highlighted as top-notch and well-stocked.

The placement record is a major source of pride, with students reporting excellent career opportunities and high-paying job roles across various industries. The institute's strong industry ties and the efforts of the Career Development Cell are recognized for shaping successful careers. The availability of numerous scholarships and financial aid, including full tuition fee waivers for economically weaker sections, is highly appreciated by students and their families, as it ensures that financial constraints do not hinder access to quality education.

The vibrant student life, including a strong hostel culture, technical and cultural festivals, and a wide array of student clubs, contributes significantly to a memorable journey. The world-class sports facilities, including an Olympic-standard swimming pool, well-equipped gyms, and various courts and grounds, are highly valued, fostering a strong sporting culture. The introduction of the Sports Excellence Admission program is also seen as a positive development. The presence of affordable eateries on campus is also a practical benefit for students. The sense of camaraderie and closeness among hostel residents, particularly in certain hostels, is also a cherished aspect of student life.

COMMON COMPLAINTS FROM STUDENTS

While IIT Madras receives widespread praise, some common complaints and areas of concern have been noted by students and alumni. One recurring sentiment is that academics can be overwhelming, indicating a high level of academic pressure and rigor that some students find challenging. Another point of contention mentioned in student reviews is inconsistent faculty quality, suggesting that while many faculty members are world-class, there might be variations in teaching effectiveness or availability across departments or individual professors.

Some students perceive the campus environment as very practical, which, while beneficial for career outcomes, might lead to a less vibrant social life or fewer events and activities compared to expectations. Compulsory attendance policies are also a source of complaint for some students.

Regarding hostel life, while generally positive, specific complaints about mess food quality are not extensively detailed in the provided snippets, but the existence of various food options suggests a diverse experience. The discretion of wardens regarding the entry of girls into boys' hostels, leading to varying freedoms across hostels, could be a point of dissatisfaction for some students.

While the campus is large and offers free electric vehicles for transport, the reliance on private bicycles for daily commute within the extensive campus might be seen as a minor inconvenience for those without one or preferring other modes.

Discrepancies between official claims and student reports are not explicitly highlighted as major issues in the provided information, but the general nature of student reviews often provides a more nuanced perspective than official reports.

The National Institute of Technology Durgapur (NIT Durgapur) is a prominent engineering institution in India, recognized as an Institute of National Importance. Established in 1960 as one of the first eight Regional Engineering Colleges (RECs), it was upgraded to an NIT in 2003. The institute is known for its academic environment, diverse student activities, and a strong alumni network.

## Placements (External View)

NIT Durgapur's placements show varying trends across different years and branches, with a strong presence of both product and service-based companies.

*   **Average, Median, Highest CTC Reported Externally (LPA)**
    *   **2025 (Projected/Reported):** The highest package reached INR 80 LPA, with an average package of INR 12.61 LPA.
    *   **2024 (B.Tech):** The highest package was ₹51 LPA, and the average package stood at ₹7.35 LPA. For Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) students, the average package was notably higher at ₹21.45 LPA.
    *   **2024 (Student Review):** The highest placement was ₹51 LPA, and the average placement was ₹7-8 LPA. For the top 10% of students, the average placement was ₹20 LPA; for the top 25%, it was ₹11 LPA; and for the top 40%, it was ₹8.5 LPA.
    *   **2023:** The highest placement was ₹70 LPA, and the average placement was ₹13 LPA. The average placement for CSE was ₹18 LPA, and the median placement was ₹8.1 LPA.
    *   **2022:** The average package offered was ₹11.46 LPA, with the average package for Computer Science Engineering being ₹18.24 LPA. The median package stood at ₹14.3 LPA. For Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE) students, the average package was ₹13.18 LPA, and the median package was ₹12.5 LPA.

*   **Placement Percentage as Reported by Students/Alumni**
    *   **2025 (Projected/Reported):** An 82% placement rate was recorded, with over 710 students placed from 210+ companies.
        *   Branch-wise placement percentages: Metallurgical and Materials Engineering (MME) - 93%, Electrical Engineering (EE) - 90%, Computer Science and Engineering (CSE) - 87%, Mechanical Engineering (ME) - 83%, Civil Engineering (CE) - 79%, Electronics and Communication Engineering (EC) - 75%, Chemical Engineering (CH) - 75%, Biotechnology (BT) - 62%.
    *   **2024 (B.Tech):** 72.08% of students were placed.
    *   **General Student Consensus:** Most branches typically see an 80%+ placement rate, with the exception of Biotechnology, which tends to struggle. MME consistently shows high placement percentages (85-90%).
    *   **2022:** 560 out of 600 students were placed.
    *   **2021:** 430 out of 600 students were placed.

*   **Top Recruiting Companies with Roles and Packages**
    *   Top recruiters include Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle, TCS, Infosys, HDFC Bank, Deloitte, PwC, JP Morgan, Google, IBM, Adobe, Apple, Publicis Sapient, Bosch, and Adani Group.
    *   Specific roles and packages for individual companies are not consistently detailed across sources, but the listed CTCs represent offers from these top firms.

*   **Internship Companies and Stipends**
    *   NIT Durgapur provides internship opportunities with leading companies such as CERN Geneva, DAAD, Microsoft, Amazon, Qualcomm, JP Morgan Chase, L&T, PWC, Sun Pharma, and Tata.
    *   On-campus internship opportunities for core branches and other courses are reported to be limited.
    *   Stipend information is not readily available in the provided sources.

*   **Product vs. Service Company Ratio**
    *   While an exact ratio is not provided, the list of recruiters includes both product-based companies (e.g., Microsoft, Amazon, Oracle, Apple, Google, IBM, Adobe, Qualcomm) and service-based companies (e.g., TCS, Infosys, Deloitte, PwC, Accenture).
    *   Student reviews suggest that most internship opportunities have historically been for IT roles, indicating a higher presence of IT/service-oriented companies for internships, especially for core branches.

*   **Student Reviews and Experiences on Placements**
    *   Students generally report good placements for most branches, with the exception of Biotechnology and Civil Engineering.
    *   The placement cell is often praised as "the best" and is maintained by faculty members.
    *   However, some students note that placements have recently dipped due to a global slowdown/recession, with CSE, ECE, and EE experiencing a significant drop in median offers. Despite this, the top 20-30% of students still secure excellent packages.
    *   Discrepancies exist, with one student review highlighting a significant drop in the average placement from ₹13 LPA in 2023 to ₹7-8 LPA in 2024 as a "concerning" issue.

*   **Any Discrepancies with Official Claims**
    *   There is a noticeable difference in the reported average CTC for 2024, with some sources stating ₹7.35 LPA and others ₹7-8 LPA, compared to ₹13 LPA in 2023. The projected 2025 average of INR 12.61 LPA suggests a recovery or different reporting methodology. Students have expressed concern over the year-on-year drop in average placements.

## Academics (Student Perspective)

*   **Quality of Teaching as Reviewed by Students**
    *   Teaching quality is generally considered good, with supportive and interactive faculty.
    *   Many professors are highly qualified, holding PhDs and possessing significant academic and real-world experience.
    *   However, some students have a mixed perception, stating that while some teachers are good, others are not fully qualified or their teaching style and behavior are not satisfactory, leading to an average faculty rating of 3.8 out of 5 stars.
    *   For first-year students, classes are often taken by research scholars and PhD students whose teaching methods can be "raw and unrefined," expecting students to understand without detailed explanations.
    *   Some professors are noted for their exceptional research work, including "Google AI scholars," while others are described as "pathetic with no teaching skills."

*   **Curriculum Relevance and Industry Alignment**
    *   The curriculum is generally considered decent but, according to some students, needs updates to align with the latest industry trends and technologies.
    *   The curriculum is regularly updated, adheres to AICTE guidelines, and incorporates electives, labs, and projects to build industry-relevant skills.
    *   The B.Tech Computer Science program's curriculum is described as "up-to-date" and covers the latest tech trends, preparing students for the industry.

*   **Difficulty Level and Academic Pressure**
    *   Semesters are generally considered difficult, and the pass percentage can be relatively low, though necessary guidance is provided.
    *   Semester exams are moderately difficult, testing conceptual clarity, with an overall pass percentage of around 85-90%.
    *   Students report academic pressure and strict adherence to a 75% attendance policy. Some core branches are noted for having particularly busy schedules.

*   **Quality of Study Material and Resources**
    *   The college boasts well-equipped labs, smart classrooms, and a central library.
    *   The library is extensive, housing 1.2 lakh volumes of books (including textbooks, reference books, and bound journals), and subscribes to approximately 180 current print journals and over 800 online journals.
    *   High-speed Wi-Fi is accessible throughout the campus.

*   **Online vs. Offline Teaching Effectiveness**
    *   Specific details on the effectiveness of online versus offline teaching are not explicitly covered in the provided search results.

## Rankings & Recognition

*   **NIRF Rank (Year-wise, All Recent Years)**
    *   **2021:** Ranked 6th among NITs and 29th overall among all Engineering Colleges in India.
    *   *More recent NIRF data was not found in the provided search results.*

*   **NAAC Grade and Score**
    *   Information regarding NIT Durgapur's NAAC grade and score was not found in the provided search results.

*   **Any International Rankings**
    *   No specific international rankings were found in the provided search results.

*   **Government Recognition or Special Status**
    *   NIT Durgapur is a National Institute of Technology, signifying its status as an Institute of National Importance.

*   **Awards or Recognitions Received**
    *   No specific awards or recognitions were detailed in the provided search results.

## Fees (Externally Reported)

*   **Actual Fees Paid by Students**
    *   **B.Tech (General Category, Family Income above ₹5 lakh):** The tuition fee is ₹62,500 per semester, totaling ₹1.25 lakh annually. Including hostel and other fees, the total annual cost is approximately ₹2.01 lakh.
    *   **General B.Tech:** The annual fee is approximately ₹2 lakhs. Other sources state B.Tech annual fees are around ₹70,000 - ₹90,000, which is considered affordable.
    *   **Overall B.Tech Program:** The total fees range between ₹5 lakh and ₹6.25 lakh.

The Indian Institute of Technology Delhi (IIT Delhi) is a premier engineering institution in India, consistently recognized for its academic rigor, research output, and strong industry connections. This report provides a comprehensive overview of IIT Delhi, drawing information from official reports, news articles, student and alumni reviews, and other credible external sources.

## Placements (External View)

IIT Delhi consistently records strong placement statistics, attracting a wide array of domestic and international recruiters across various sectors. While official reports often highlight high placement rates and lucrative packages, student and alumni perspectives, along with some news reports, offer a more nuanced view, occasionally pointing to challenges and discrepancies.

*   **Average, Median, Highest CTC Reported Externally (LPA)**
    *   **Highest Package:**
        *   The highest package reported for IIT Delhi has reached **INR 4 Crore** (from a student review for the CS department in 2026).
        *   Other reports indicate a highest overall package of **INR 2.4 Crore** in 2025 and **INR 2 Crore** in 2025.
        *   The highest international package was **INR 2 Crore** in 2023 and **INR 1.5 Crore** in 2025.
        *   The highest domestic package was above **INR 1 Crore** per annum in 2023.
        *   For B.Tech CSE, the highest package was **INR 1.2 Crore** in 2025, while for M.Tech, it was **INR 1.2 Crore** in 2025.
        *   MBA students received a highest package of **INR 43.55 LPA** in 2025.
    *   **Average Package:**
        *   The overall average salary for IIT Delhi graduates is reported to be around **INR 25.1 LPA**, based on 2784 profiles. Another overall average for 2025 was **INR 27.54 LPA**.
        *   For B.Tech students, the average package is projected to be around **INR 20-22 LPA** in 2026, an increase from **INR 18.5 LPA** in 2023. The average for B.Tech in 2025 was **INR 27 LPA**.
        *   M.Tech students are projected to have an average package of **INR 25-28 LPA** in 2026, with **INR 28.2 LPA** reported for 2025.
        *   MBA graduates saw an average package of **INR 22.53 LPA** in 2025 and **INR 23.4 LPA** in 2025. In 2023, the average for MBA was **INR 25.82 LPA**, up from **INR 21.9 LPA** in 2022 and **INR 18.5 LPA** in 2021.
        *   Branch-wise averages in 2025 include: Computer Science & Engineering at **INR 43.12 LPA**, Mathematics & Computing at **INR 39.56 LPA**, Electrical Engineering at **INR 30.25 LPA**, Mechanical Engineering at **INR 22.80 LPA**, Chemical Engineering at **INR 21.10 LPA**, Civil Engineering at **INR 20.15 LPA**, Engineering Physics at **INR 25.40 LPA**, Textile Technology at **INR 17.55 LPA**, and Biochemical & Biotechnology at **INR 18.70 LPA**.
        *   For M.Tech Energy Systems Engineering, the average package was **INR 14 LPA** in 2023 and **INR 13.65 LPA** in 2022.
    *   **Median Package:**
        *   The median salary for UG (4-year) programs was **INR 19.08 LPA** in 2024 (as per NIRF 2025 report).
        *   UG (5-year) programs recorded a median package of **INR 24.3 LPA** in 2024.
        *   For PG (2-year) engineering programs (M.Tech), the median package was **INR 15.59 LPA** in 2024, increasing from **INR 14 LPA** in 2023 and **INR 12.5 LPA** in 2022.
        *   PG (2-year) management programs (MBA) had a median package of **INR 22.05 LPA** in 2024, up from **INR 20.06 LPA** in 2021-22. The median for MBA in 2025 was **INR 22.51 LPA**.
        *   The overall median salary in the previous season (2024-25) was **INR 19.10 LPA**.
        *   In 2022-23, the median salary for IIT Delhi was **INR 20 LPA**.
*   **Placement Percentage as Reported by Students/Alumni**
    *   IIT Delhi aims for near **100% placement rates**, especially for programs like Computer Science Engineering.
    *   Student opinions suggest placement rates of approximately **90-100%** for most programs.
    *   For the CS department, a student reported **95%** placement.
    *   Mathematics & Computing students also report placement percentages above **90%**.
    *   However, official data for the ongoing 2024-25 season showed a **61%** overall placement rate with 1,147 students placed out of 1,885 registered as of December 31, 2024.
    *   The B.Tech placement rate in 2024 was around **83.5%** as per the NIRF 2025 report.
    *   The MBA placement rate was **98%** in 2025 and **100%** in 2023 and 2024.
    *   The placement percentage for B.Tech students was **89.41%** in 2023-24.
    *   In 2024, 66% of UG 4-year students, 80% of UG 5-year students, and 47% of PG 2-year engineering students were placed.
*   **Top Recruiting Companies with Roles and Packages**
    *   **Tech Giants:** Google (50+ offers, average INR 30 LPA), Microsoft (40 offers, AI/ML focus), Amazon, Oracle, Adobe, Qualcomm, Intel, Texas Instruments. Roles include data analyst, ML engineer, backend engineer, and frontend engineer.
    *   **Consulting Firms:** McKinsey & Company, Boston Consulting Group (BCG), Bain & Company, EY, Accenture Strategy and Consulting, Alvarez & Marsal, Acuvon Consulting, Axtria. BCG and Bain offered strategy positions at INR 25-35 LPA.
    *   **Finance & Trading:** Goldman Sachs (finance quant roles), JP Morgan Chase, Barclays, American Express, Graviton Research Capital, Squarepoint Capital, Jane Street, Optiver. Goldman Sachs finance roles hit INR 35 LPA.
    *   **Core Engineering/Manufacturing:** Tata Steel, Reliance Industries (packages often above ₹18 LPA), L&T, Air India, Bajaj Auto, Ola Electric, Schlumberger, Micron Technology, Sterlite Group, Trident Group.
    *   **Other Prominent Recruiters:** TCS, Infosys (100+ offers), Atrenta, Cadence Design Systems, Capital One Financial Services, Caterpillar, Deloitte, Shell, HSBC, KPMG, Reckitt Benckiser, Michael Page, GE Healthcare, Nestle, HDFC Bank, Boston Scientific, Paytm, Flipkart, Meesho, Navi, Nine Education, PayU Payments, Shiprocket, Turing Global India Pvt. Ltd., Wells Fargo International Solutions Pvt Ltd.
    *   PSUs like IOCL and BPCL also recruit.
*   **Internship Companies and Stipends**
    *   **IIT Delhi Summer Research Fellowship:** Offers a stipend of **₹2,000 per week**, along with reimbursement for sleeper-class train travel within India, free hostel accommodation, boarding, and lodging. This program is for students from *other* engineering institutes, typically for an 8-week duration (e.g., May 13 to July 13, 2026).
    *   **Central Library Internship:** Offers a consolidated monthly stipend of **₹30,000** for a one-year full-time internship. Institute accommodation is not provided. A separate program for MLIS students as part of their academic curriculum offers no stipend or accommodation.
    *   **DMS (MBA) Summer Placements:** For the 2021-23 batch, the highest stipend reached **INR 4 Lakhs**, with an average of **INR 1.43 Lakhs**. For the MBA batch of 2024, the highest stipend was **INR 4.04 Lakhs per month**, and the average was **INR 2.63 Lakhs per month**.
    *   **High-Paying Internships:** Companies like Jane Street are known to offer "insane money" for internships, particularly to students with strong math backgrounds, competitive coding skills, and high GPAs, often for roles like Quant strategists or C++ developers.
    *   Historically, international internships from companies like Microsoft Redmond (USA), Uber (USA), Oracle (USA), and Samsung (South Korea) have offered packages around **INR 1.2 Crore PA** (2014 data). Domestic high-paying internships in 2014 included Tower Research (40 LPA) and Goldman Sachs (31 LPA).
*   **Product vs Service Company Ratio**
    *   The **Core (Technical) sector** consistently emerges as the top recruiting sector, accounting for **34%** of total offers in 2025 and 2025-26. It also comprised about **42%** of placements until Phase 1 of the 2024 placement session.
    *   The **IT sector** followed with **20%** of total offers in 2025 and 2025-26.
    *   **Consulting** accounted for **14%** of offers in 2025 and 2025-26.
    *   The **Management sector** made up **13%** of offers in 2025.
    *   For MBA placements in 2024, Strategy & Consulting was the most favored domain with **24.4%** of offers, followed by IT & Analytics with **19.2%**.

PLACEMENTS

Symbiosis Institute of Technology, Pune, maintains a very well-organized placement and training cell. The infrastructure within the placement cell includes a seminar hall specifically designed for conducting pre-placement talks, along with dedicated discussion rooms, interview rooms, and other necessary amenities to facilitate the recruitment process. The cell has established strong associations with a large number of renowned companies that regularly visit the institute for campus recruitments. All students in their final year are thoroughly prepared for campus interviews through specialized programmes focusing on both technical and soft skills, which are crucial for securing prestigious jobs. SIT has consistently experienced successful placement seasons, marked by the participation of leading companies across various sectors, offering highly coveted profiles to both B.Tech and M.Tech students. The recruiter portfolio is characterized by a healthy mix of companies from IT sectors and fast-growing start-ups. Furthermore, a select number of students, demonstrating exceptional effort and performance during their internships and participation in reputed corporate competitions, have been awarded pre-placement offers (PPOs) by highly coveted companies.

The placement records for Symbiosis Institute of Technology, Pune, provide detailed information on student success. For the year 2025-26, as on date, the placement percentage is greater than 80%, with the highest package offered reaching 27 LPA, and the highest internship stipend offered being 85 K/Month. In the academic year 2024-25, the placement percentage stood at 92%, the highest package offered was 24 LPA, and the highest internship stipend offered was 75 K/Month. For the academic year 2023-24, the placement percentage was 91%, the highest package offered was an impressive 50 LPA, and the highest internship stipend offered was 75 K/Month.

The year 2024-25 witnessed the presence of more than 215 companies, which included a diverse blend of IT and ITES companies, Consultancy firms, Manufacturing Units, Digital marketing firms, and Edtech companies. Notable recruiters during this period included Workday, Nvidia, UKG, Microsoft, IBM India Pvt Ltd, Nomura Services India Pvt Ltd, BMC Software, Bharat Forge, Kalyani Group, Juspay, HP Inc, Promobi Technologies, AP Moller, FutureFirst, ZS Associates, MiQ Digital India Pvt Ltd, Miniorange Security Software Pvt Ltd, Deloitte, Lubrizol Corporation, SAS R&D, Intuitive Cloud, Deloitte Tax, Deloitte Audit, KION Group, Forma.ai, Precisely, Tresvista, Baker Hughes, Isuzu, Buyhatke, Oracle, Forbes Marshall, and Hyundai Motors, among many others. For the year 2025-26, the placement process has commenced in full swing, with some of the top companies from the aforementioned list having already visited the campus and recruited students. The placement cum internship process for the 2025 batch of B.Tech and M.Tech students has been initiated, with several companies of repute participating. These include A P Moller, Aeron Systems, Bajaj Finserv, Barclay's, Bharat Forge, BMC, Clarity, Deloitte, Exide Industries, Fisher Jordan Upgrad, Future First, HDFC Life, HP, IBM ISL, JM Finance, John Deere, Juspay, Kohinoor Group, Lubrizol, Microsoft, MiQ Digital India Pvt Ltd, Nomura Services India Pvt Ltd, Oracle, Philips India Pvt Ltd, Rockwell Automation, Stonex, UKG, Unbox Robotics, UpGrad, Vanderlande, Varroc, Veltrik.EV, Workday, and ZScaler, with many more expected to participate.

The Department of Training and Placements at Symbiosis Institute of Technology Pune is responsible for handling the campus placement of B.Tech and M.Tech graduating students across all engineering campuses. The Placement Cell offers comprehensive support to visiting companies at every stage of the placement process. This includes making arrangements for Pre-Placement Talks, Written Tests, Interviews, and Group Discussions, all tailored to the specific requirements of the visiting companies. The objectives of the Department of Training and Placements are to facilitate campus recruitment opportunities with reputed organizations in India and abroad for B.Tech and M.Tech students, to enhance student employability through structured training in aptitude, technical skills, communication, personality development, and career guidance provided by industry experts, to maintain regular interactions with the industry through Seminars, Guest Lectures, Conferences, and Corporate Meets, and to collaborate with industry for Live projects, Research work, Industrial visits, Workshops, or any other academic alliances.

The placements policy for final placements stipulates that a student can apply to any number of companies, whether in IT or Core sectors. However, upon receiving two offers, the student would be considered out of the placement processes. To avail a second offer, a student must satisfy the criteria of the '2x rule', which mandates that the Cost to Company (CTC) as quoted by recruiters for the second offer must be two times the CTC of the first offer. Eligibility for the placement process is determined by the individual student's academic performance and the specific criteria laid down by the recruiting company. All communication between companies and students, and vice versa, is routed through the Training and Placement office. Students are required to notify the Training and Placement office if they choose to opt out of the final placement process for personal reasons or to pursue higher education. It is important to note that the role of the Training and Placement office is that of a facilitator and counsellor for placement related activities, and it does not guarantee a job.

The Training and Placement Committee Members include Dr. Nilisha Itankar, who serves as the Head of Placements, reachable via email at placements@sitpune.edu.in and by phone at (020)28116442 or 9860147596. Dr. Ravi Sekhar is a Faculty Incharge, with email ravi.sekhar@sitpune.edu.in and phone numbers (020)28116510 or 9764004681. Rahul Digge is a Training & Placements Officer, contactable at tpo@sitpune.edu.in and (020)28116513 or 9623477077. Pushkar Gohel is also a Training & Placements Officer, with email pushkar.gohel@sitpune.edu.in and phone numbers (020)28116305 or 9972226680. Rashmi Kshirsagar holds the position of Senior Supervisor, and can be reached at rashmi.kshirsagar@sitpune.edu.in and (020)28116443 or 9822326886. The general contact email for placements is placements@sitpune.edu.in and tpo@sitpune.edu.in. The general phone numbers for the placement cell are 020 - 2811 6300, 6442, 6513, and 6510.

The Project Semester is a significant component of the curriculum, involving a six-month duration internship in industry. During this period, students undertake projects and are expected to complete them to the full satisfaction of the industry. The emphasis of the project semester is on undertaking projects and problem-solving within an industrial setting. The concept of a six-month internship stems from the realization that shorter internships, typically 6 to 8 weeks, are insufficient for any meaningful and effective learning on the part of students. Similarly, for the industry, short internships are not as useful as students are often unable to contribute significantly within such a limited timeframe. The Project Semester programme of SIT has been meticulously designed and monitored to ensure it benefits all stakeholders: the students, the institute, and the industry. Students undertake projects under the guidance of both an industry mentor and a faculty mentor. The faculty member closely monitors the progress of the students and undertakes at least two visits to the concerned industry. At the conclusion of the term, a joint evaluation is conducted, either at the Institute or within the industry.

The objectives of the Project Semester are to expose students to real-life working conditions in the industry and the practical application of theoretical knowledge gained in classes. It also aims to inculcate problem-solving skills among students using a systematic approach, and to sensitize them about the importance of adhering to time limits for completing projects. Furthermore, the programme seeks to create a mutually beneficial scheme for both the industry and the academic institutes, where students and the Institute benefit in terms of practical knowledge and skills, and the industry benefits by utilizing students on various projects.

Utmost care is taken to ensure the quality of the project semester programme through several steps. The choice of the industry is made very carefully, considering the standing and status of the company, the availability of suitable projects, the company's willingness to deploy students on these projects, and its faith in the institute and students regarding their capability to successfully complete these projects. Once a student is placed in an organization, the institute maintains regular contact with him or her and monitors their performance. For this purpose, a faculty member is appointed as an internal mentor, and a mentor is designated from the industry. The faculty mentor visits the industry twice during the project semester of the students and evaluates their performance. During these visits, the faculty mentor monitors the progress of the student and evaluates him or her using a designated performa, also meeting with seniors in the industry to gather their feedback for evaluation. Towards the end of the internship, a joint evaluation is carried out either in the industry or in the institute.

The departmental faculty in-charges for internships are: for CSE/IT/AIML, Dr. Sonali Kothari and Dr. Sudhanshu Gonge, who can be reached at sonali.tidke@sitpune.edu.in and sudhanshu.gonge@sitpune.edu.in respectively, or by phone at 02039116455. For E&TC, Prof. Kunal Shejul is the in-charge, reachable at kunal.shejul@sitpune.edu.in or by phone at 02061936474. For Mechanical Engineering, Dr. Ravi Shekhar is the in-charge, contactable at ravi.sekhar@sitpune.edu.in or by phone at 02061936437. For Civil Engineering, Prof. Humera Khanum is the in-charge, reachable at Humera.khanum@sitpune.edu.in or by phone at 02039116483.

The procedure for internships is as follows: The Institute will arrange internships in various organizations. Students will be allotted internships in a company based on merit or any other criterion laid down by the company. In some cases, students may be allowed to arrange their own internships. In such instances, a student can obtain a letter from the placement or respective department and then contact the company. The confirmation letter from the company must then be submitted to the placement or respective department. Students will be associated with one faculty member from their respective department who will act as an internal mentor. During the six-month duration, the internal mentor will assess the student's performance twice. The final evaluation of the internship will be conducted jointly by the internal mentor and the company mentor. Students are required to maintain a record of the work done in the industry and submit a report to the institute within one week of the start of the next semester. The certificate and the report must be duly signed by a responsible official of the company. The institute will arrange the evaluation of the internship within 15 days of the start of the semester, and the date of evaluation will be notified at least one week before the scheduled date. In cases where companies visit the institute to select students for internships, all regulations pertaining to 'placements' will be applicable for such internships.

external.text:
Symbiosis Institute of Technology (SIT) in Pune, India, is a constituent of Symbiosis International (Deemed University) and has established itself as a prominent engineering institution. The institute focuses on providing quality education aligned with industry demands and technological advancements, fostering an environment conducive to learning and harnessing the potential of both faculty and students. SIT Pune is recognized for its commitment to empowering students for success and providing rewarding career pathways.

PLACEMENTS

Symbiosis Institute of Technology Pune has a robust placement record, with consistent high placement rates and increasing compensation benchmarks across various engineering streams. The institute's placement cell actively works to make students industry-ready.

Placement Statistics and Packages:
The placement process for 2026 was ongoing as of February 2026. The highest international package offered during SIT Pune placements in 2026 was INR 85 LPA, marking an increase of over 13% compared to 2025. The highest domestic package offered in 2026 was INR 27 LPA, also showing an increase of nearly 13%. As of February 2026, the placement percentage recorded for 2026 was 75%. Over 215 recruiters had visited the campus for the 2026 placement drive.

For the 2025 placement drive, the overall highest international package offered was 75 LPA, and the highest domestic package was INR 21 LPA. The average package offered in 2025 was INR 8.91 LPA. The placement percentage for 2025 stood at 92%. In 2024, the overall average package offered was INR 12.97 LPA, and the placement percentage was 91%. The highest package offered to B.Tech students in 2024 was INR 50 LPA, with an average B.Tech package of INR 10.70 LPA. The M.Tech highest package in 2024 was INR 12.60 LPA, and the M.Tech average package was INR 8.58 LPA.

For the 2023-2024 academic year, SIT Pune announced a highest package of INR 50 LPA and an average package of INR 9.32 LPA. The institute achieved an impressive 91% placement rate for the 2023-2024 batch. Over 175 companies participated in this placement drive. In 2023, the highest package was INR 36.5 LPA, and the median package was INR 12 LPA.

In 2022, 97% of engineering students were placed, with an average package of INR 6 LPA. The highest salary package in 2022 was INR 42 LPA, offered to a Computer Science student.

Student-reported data indicates some discrepancies. While official reports mention a highest package of 50 LPA in 2023, some students claim that the highest on-campus package was 11 LPA, with higher figures being off-campus offers where the college played no direct role. However, other student reviews corroborate the 50 LPA figure as the highest paycheck from SIT in 2023.

Year-wise Placement Statistics:
*   **2026 (ongoing till Feb 2026):** Highest International Package: INR 85 LPA; Highest Domestic Package: INR 27 LPA; Placement Percentage: 75%; Recruiters: 215+
*   **2025:** Highest International Package: 75 LPA; Highest Domestic Package: INR 21 LPA; Average Package: INR 8.91 LPA; Placement Percentage: 92%; Recruiters: 130 companies.
*   **2024:** Highest Package (B.Tech): INR 50 LPA; Average Package (Overall): INR 12.97 LPA; Average Package (B.Tech): INR 10.70 LPA; Highest Package (M.Tech): INR 12.60 LPA; Average Package (M.Tech): INR 8.58 LPA; Placement Percentage: 91%.
*   **2023-2024:** Highest Domestic Package: INR 50 LPA; Average Package: INR 9.3 LPA; Placement Rate: 91%.
*   **2022:** Highest Package: INR 42 LPA; Average Package: INR 6 LPA; Placement Percentage: 97%.
*   **2016-17:** Highest Salary Package: 9.78 LPA by Microsoft.

Branch-wise B.Tech Placement Data (2025, from Mandatory Disclosure):
*   B.Tech CSE: 114 students placed out of 167 eligible students.
*   B.Tech AI & ML: 56 students placed out of 111 eligible students.
*   M.Tech AI & ML: 17 students placed out of 29 eligible students.

Recruiting Companies:
Over 200 recruiters have visited the campus over the past three years. Top recruiters include Palo Alto, Microsoft, Philips, PhonePe, Nvidia, Oracle, Capgemini, Deloitte, Infosys, TCS, Wipro, Accenture, Amazon, IBM, Indeed, Dassault, Bajaj Finserv Group, GE Aviation, A P Moller, MIQ Digital, Mobisoft, Adenza, Parker Digital, Siemens, MG Motors, Juspay, and BMC. Companies like Microsoft, Google, Amazon, Federal Bank, and Amdocs have also visited the campus. Other frequent recruiters mentioned by students include Cognizant, Hexaware, and Tech Mahindra.

Specific Roles Offered:
While specific roles are not exhaustively detailed for each company, the institute prepares students for diverse opportunities in IT, Core Engineering, Finance & Banking, Ed-Tech, Media, Marketing, and the Service Industry. Students also secure roles in AI/ML startups.

Most Frequent Recruiters:
Infosys and Deloitte are frequently mentioned as consistent recruiters.

Pre-Placement Offers:
Information specifically on pre-placement offers is not explicitly detailed in the provided search results.

International Placements:
SIT Pune offers international placements. The highest international package offered in 2026 was INR 85 LPA. In 2025 and 2024, the highest international package offered was 75 LPA. Another source mentions a highest international package of 29 LPA for 2025. One report from July 2025 states the highest international package secured by students so far is 1600 USD.

Internship Placements:
About 60% of students get internships through campus or by self-application, with companies like Siemens and Persistent. Internships are initiated from the third year, with students eligible for placement from the fourth year. Some sources indicate internships start from the 6th semester. The institute emphasizes internships, with a dedicated semester for practical exposure. Companies also contribute to internship projects, recruiting interns for the period from April to June every year.

Student Reviews and Experiences about the Placement Process:
Student reviews indicate strong placement statistics, particularly for Computer Science (CS) and Information Technology (IT) branches, with reported placement rates of 90-100%. Students generally find the placement scenario for CSE promising, especially for those who actively develop their skills. However, Mechanical and Civil branches reportedly face challenges with lower placement rates, with one review highlighting a 9% placement rate for Mechanical in 2018-19.

Some students express concerns about discrepancies between official claims and actual on-campus placements, noting that higher packages might be off-campus offers. Despite this, many students find SIT a good place for direct placements in companies like Wipro, Cognizant, Hexaware, and TCS. The placement cell is noted for honoring students' skills to make them industry-ready.

Placement Cell Contact:
Specific email addresses or phone numbers for the placement cell were not readily available in the provided search results.

ACADEMICS AND CURRICULUM

Quality of Academics:
The quality of academics at SIT Pune is generally regarded as solid, with a focus on providing a good grasp of fundamentals. Student reviews often praise the academic environment. The institute aims to provide quality education in line with industry requirements and rapid technological developments.

Programs Offered:
SIT Pune offers programs at Undergraduate (UG), Postgraduate (PG), and Doctoral levels in Engineering and Technology.
*   **B.Tech Branches:**
    *   Computer Science and Engineering (CSE)
    *   Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (AI & ML)
    *   Electronics and Telecommunication Engineering (E&TC)
    *   Mechanical Engineering
    *   Civil Engineering
    *   Robotics and Automation
    *   Computer Engineering (CE)
    *   Computer Science and Technology (CST)
    *   Robotics and Artificial Intelligence (RAI)
*   **M.Tech Specializations:** Specific specializations are not explicitly listed beyond M.Tech AI & ML, but the institute offers M.Tech programs generally.
*   **PhD Programs:** SIT Pune offers PhD programs.

Curriculum Quality:
The curriculum is described as updated, industry-relevant, and designed to meet the needs of the industry, training students accordingly. It is reviewed and updated yearly to stay relevant and make students industry-ready. The program structure focuses on both fundamentals and current advancements, allowing students to build a strong foundation and stay updated with the latest developments. The CSE department's teaching quality is specifically noted for helping make students industry-ready. Some student feedback suggests that while the curriculum is relevant, it could be even more industry-oriented.

Examination System, Grading, Academic Pressure:
The semester exams are generally considered moderate to hard but are beneficial for students. Students report that exams are easy if one studies for even two weeks. There are continuous assessments, which encourage students to frequently brush up on their syllabus, and examinations are held under strict vigilance. Professors also assign mini-projects, which can be individual or team-led. The pass percentage is around 80-70%.

Quality of Study Material, Access to Online Resources, E-learning Platforms:
The library and labs are described as very good, with all necessary apparatus available. The labs are well-equipped. The institute facilitates Value-Added Certification Programs in collaboration with global companies to enhance global employability and technical competence. These certifications provide access to industry-recognized certifications that validate skills and align with international standards. The institute also uses platforms like Codetantra for skill enhancement courses.

Faculty Quality from Student Perspective:
Faculty members are generally described as supportive, helpful, and knowledgeable. Most faculty members are PhD holders from reputable institutes. They are easy to approach and willing to assist with higher studies preparation. Building a rapport with teachers is considered beneficial for guidance and support. The teaching quality, especially in the CSE department, is good. Teachers are also noted for assisting in writing and publishing research papers. Some students mention that teachers are very helpful if students show a genuine desire to learn.

Academic Rigor and Comparison to Peer Institutions:
SIT Pune's CSE program is considered a strong option for students seeking a blend of academic rigor and industry exposure. The institute's rigorous training programs and industry-relevant curriculum contribute to its academic standing.

Special Academic Programs, Honors, Minors, Industry Tie-up Courses:
The institute fosters a culture of creativity and problem-solving through its Entrepreneurship Promotion & Innovation Centre (EPIC) and the Infosys MAKER LAB. Programs include hackathons, pitchfests, boot camps, and innovation challenges. The curriculum integrates AI/ML, Data Science, Cybersecurity, and IoT, with project-based learning. Students are encouraged to learn other subjects like French, German, disaster management, and first-aid training.

Attendance Policies:
Attendance policies are implemented, and faculty members appointed as mentors for every 20 students are responsible for ensuring student attendance and academic performance.

RANKINGS AND RECOGNITION

NIRF Ranking:
SIT Pune has consistently featured in the NIRF rankings.
*   **NIRF Engineering Ranking 2025:** 46th position.
*   **NIRF Engineering Ranking 2024:** 59th position.
*   **NIRF Engineering Ranking 2023:** 68th position.
*   **NIRF Engineering Ranking 2022:** 83rd position.

Specific NIRF score breakdowns were not available in the provided search results.

NAAC Accreditation:
Symbiosis International (Deemed University), of which SIT Pune is a constituent, has been re-accredited by NAAC with an 'A++ Grade'. SIT Pune itself holds NAAC A++ accreditation.

NBA Accreditation:
SIT Pune is accredited by NBA. The CSE department is NBA-accredited. Specific cycles of accreditation were not detailed.

International Rankings:
Symbiosis International (Deemed University) has received various international rankings, including:
*   SIU's U.S. News Best Global Universities Rankings 2025.
*   Times Higher Education (THE) Asia University Rankings.
*   QS Ranking (SIU) India, Asia and World 2026.
*   QS Asia Rankings 2026 among Private – Not for Profit Institutions.
